questions.q: Where does the indexer sit in the game-piece path?
wrong: Before the intake pulls pieces in
After the flywheel launches a piece
Inside the drivetrain's main gearbox
questions.explain: The path is intake → storage → indexer → flywheel. The indexer feeds stored pieces up to the spinning flywheel to be launched.

questions.q: What kind of servo is the indexer's feeder?
wrong: A positional servo that holds an angle
A DcMotorEx with a built-in encoder
A stepper motor with fine little steps
questions.explain: The feeder is a CRServo — it just spins at a speed, like a little motor. It uses setPower(), not an angle like a positional servo.

questions.q: How does a CRServo differ from a positional servo?
questions.correct: A CRServo sets a speed, not a held angle
wrong: A CRServo holds an exact angle and stays
A CRServo is powered by its own battery
A CRServo can only ever spin one way
questions.explain: A positional servo goes to an exact angle and holds (a "Pointer"); a CRServo just spins at a speed (a "Spinner"). The feeder needs to spin, so it's a CRServo.

questions.q: How do you drive a CRServo in code?
wrong: feeder.setPosition(value), like an angle
feeder.setAngle(value), given in degrees
feeder.spinForever(value), only once
questions.explain: A CRServo uses setPower() from -1.0 to 1.0, just like a motor — 1.0 full one way, -1.0 the other, 0.0 stop. There's no angle to set.

questions.q: The indexer's state machine has how many states?
wrong: Three: forward, off, and reverse
Four: stowed, raising, holding, lowering
One: it only ever keeps feeding
questions.explain: The indexer is a simple two-state machine — a boolean feeding that's either true or false. Simpler than the intake's three-state enum.

questions.correct: Once, when the Robot builds the indexer
wrong: Every loop, about 50 times a second
Only when the X button is pressed
After the match has completely ended
questions.explain: The constructor runs once at build time to find the feeder servo. update() is what runs every loop. Once for setup, forever for use.

questions.q: Feeding the shooter is a "hold," which means...
questions.correct: It feeds while X is held and stops when released
wrong: One press feeds forever until you press again
A single press feeds exactly one piece each time
It feeds only during the autonomous phase
questions.explain: Feeding is a hold: while X is down, feed; when it's up, stop. That's different from the intake's press-to-toggle behavior.

questions.q: Does a hold-to-feed button need edge detection?
questions.correct: No — a plain if (gamepad1.x) is correct
wrong: Yes — without it the feeder never runs
Yes — otherwise it feeds much too fast
No — but only during autonomous mode
questions.explain: Holds don't need edge detection; you want it to feed the whole time X is held. Edge detection is for toggles, where one press flips a state once.

questions.q: What is a logic guard like if (feeder == null) return;?
questions.correct: A check that handles a special case and returns early
wrong: A command that spins the feeder at full speed
A line that prints the feeder's current state
A loop that waits for the feeder to warm up
questions.explain: A guard checks a special case first (here, no feeder configured) and returns early so the rest of the method is safely skipped. It prevents crashes.

questions.q: What does the ternary feeding ? FEED_POWER : 0.0 do?
questions.correct: Picks one of two values based on feeding
wrong: Adds FEED_POWER and 0.0 together
Loops until feeding becomes true
Prints feeding to the telemetry line
questions.explain: The ternary reads "if feeding, use FEED_POWER, else 0.0." It's a compact if/else that produces the power to send to the servo.

questions.correct: Whether the indexer is currently feeding
wrong: How many pieces have been fed so far
The exact speed of the feeder servo
The robot's current heading angle value
questions.explain: isFeeding() returns the boolean feeding — true while feeding, false otherwise. It lets the OpMode show the state on telemetry.

questions.q: If you put edge detection on the hold-to-feed button...
questions.correct: You'd have to tap repeatedly to keep feeding
wrong: The feeder servo would spin twice as fast
The robot's battery would last much longer
The servo would hold one exact angle
questions.explain: Edge detection fires once per press, so a hold-to-feed button with edge detection would only feed for a single loop per tap — ruining the smooth hold.

questions.q: If the feeder never moves, a likely cause is...
questions.correct: The indexer wasn't added to the scheduler list
wrong: The battery is charged a little too much
The telemetry is printing far too many lines
The A button was pressed instead of the X
questions.explain: If update() never runs (the indexer isn't in subsystems), the servo is never told to spin. Adding it to the scheduler list fixes that.

questions.q: The commands feed() and stop() change...
questions.correct: The feeding field, not the servo directly
wrong: The servo power, skipping the field
The robot's heading from the IMU
The telemetry text on the screen
questions.explain: feed() sets feeding = true and stop() sets it false. update() reads that field and drives the servo. Commands decide; update() does.

questions.q: Why does the indexer feed WHILE X is held?
questions.correct: So pieces flow steadily up to the flywheel
wrong: So the flywheel spins at a higher RPM
So the battery charges between the shots
So the robot strafes toward the hive
questions.explain: Holding X runs the feeder continuously, pushing stored pieces into the spinning flywheel for a steady stream of shots. Release to stop feeding.
